agenda: Reports of the Secretary-General on the Sudan and South Sudan
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our objective is to secure a one-year renewal of UNMISS with robust protection of civilians, unimpeded humanitarian access, accountability for the Old Fangak hospital airstrike, and support for credible electoral preparations. We expect the most difficult negotiations to concern specific condemnations and accountability language, as well as human rights and electoral tasks, which Russia and China may seek to dilute. We are prepared to negotiate reasonable compromises, but we will insist that the mandate remain robust enough to address the current crisis and attract at least nine votes without a veto.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of UNMISS and the draft's emphasis on protection of civilians and respect for South Sudan's sovereignty. We ask that the mandate be implemented in full respect for national ownership and in close coordination with the Government of South Sudan, the African Union and IGAD. We also request a preambular reference to reviewing the South Sudan sanctions regime, particularly the arms embargo, so that it does not hinder implementation of the Revitalised Agreement and national security capacity-building.
messages.China: China supports the timely extension of UNMISS to avoid a mandate gap, but the text should more clearly reflect host-state ownership, consent and close consultation with the Government of South Sudan. We propose adding respect for South Sudan's sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity and consultation with its Government in OP1, and adjusting OP3 so that the investigation language does not prejudge responsibility and calls on all parties to cooperate. China also asks that the political and electoral language be explicitly South Sudanese-led and anchored in the Revitalised Agreement and national framework.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the renewal of UNMISS and welcomes the penholder's draft. We ask that the Council strengthen accountability in OP3 and OP2(c), use standard WPS language on women's full, equal and meaningful participation, and make the concern over arms flows operative and reportable in OP6/OP7. These changes would strengthen implementation without delaying the renewal.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of UNMISS and thanks the United States for the draft. We would like the text to be strengthened on accountability for the attack on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak, on unhindered access to affected areas, and on the regional dimension, including arms flows. With these limited changes, France is ready to support the resolution.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of UNMISS and the draft as circulated. We welcome its strong emphasis on protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access, accountability for the attack on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak, and inclusive political dialogue. Given the imminent expiry of the mandate, Greece encourages the Council to proceed swiftly to adoption.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of UNMISS and the robust protection mandate reflected in the draft. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP3 by providing for an independent and impartial investigation with UNMISS support where appropriate, and to add reporting on arms flows and external interference. We also suggest strengthening OP7 reporting on humanitarian access and implementation of the Revitalised Agreement, including women's and youth participation.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft resolution as circulated and welcomes the one-year extension of UNMISS's mandate. We believe the text appropriately prioritizes protection of civilians, humanitarian access and support for the Revitalised Agreement, while reaffirming South Sudan's sovereignty and primary responsibility. Given the imminent expiry of the mandate, we urge the Council to adopt the text promptly and speak with one voice.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of UNMISS with a robust protection of civilians and humanitarian access mandate. We ask the penholder to add explicit language on the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society in political and electoral processes, and on respect for the Status of Forces Agreement and UNMISS freedom of movement. With these changes, Panama can support the draft.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of UNMISS and the draft’s focus on protection of civilians, humanitarian access and accountability. We would like OP3 to require that the investigation’s findings be reported to the Council, and OP4 to include an explicit demand that the Government of South Sudan respect UNMISS freedom of movement and the Status of Forces Agreement. We also suggest OP6 explicitly call for compliance with the arms embargo on South Sudan, given reports of cross-border arms flows.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the extension of UNMISS but considers the current text overly prescriptive. We request a clear clause on South Sudan's sovereignty and host-state consent, removal of vague 'robust action' and intrusive accountability language, and amendment of OP3 so that investigations are requested of all parties rather than singling out the Government. We also ask to delete the unverified reference to 'reports of arms flows' in PP6.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of UNMISS and the robust protection-of-civilians and humanitarian access tasks in the draft. We ask the penholder to strengthen accountability follow-up to the 3 May attack on the MSF hospital by ensuring an independent investigation with UNMISS and UN human rights support and by requiring the Secretary-General to report on it, arms flows and cross-border displacement. We also see value in explicitly including civil society in the political dialogue and electoral preparations.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the renewal of UNMISS and the robust protection and access provisions in the draft. We ask the penholder to strengthen accountability for the Old Fangak hospital attack through an independent investigation supported by UNMISS and reporting to the Council, to add grave violations against children to the human rights monitoring task, and to make OP6 explicit on preventing arms transfers that fuel the conflict. These changes would align the text with the Council’s responsibility to protect civilians and with Slovenia’s consistent position on accountability and international humanitarian law.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the extension of UNMISS and strongly condemns the attack on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak. We ask the penholder to strengthen host-state and regional ownership by referencing close coordination with the Government of South Sudan, the African Union and IGAD, and to ensure the investigation is conducted with UN support and that all parties cooperate. We also request that reporting reflect coordination with the African Union and IGAD. These changes would reinforce the mandate's legitimacy and effectiveness on the ground.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the draft and strongly supports renewal of UNMISS. We would like the investigation into the Old Fangak hospital attack to be independent and UNMISS-supported, and for the text to demand full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement and an end to movement restrictions. We also ask that OP6 make clear that all States must comply with the arms embargo and refrain from arms transfers that fuel the conflict, and that OP5 include civic space.

replies.Algeria: partially accepted: added full respect/primary responsibility and coordination with the Government, AU and IGAD, plus a sanctions-review preambular paragraph with compliance emphasis.
replies.China: accepted: OP1 reflects sovereignty, territorial integrity, consent and close consultation; OP2(e), OP3 and OP6 incorporate South Sudanese ownership, cooperation and non-interference.
replies.Denmark: accepted: accountability/evidence language, full equal and meaningful participation, arms embargo compliance and reporting included.
replies.France: accepted: access includes Old Fangak and Upper Nile; OP3 cooperation/access, OP6 arms transfers and sovereignty, and OP7 regional impact included.
replies.Guyana: partially accepted: OP3 independent/impartial investigation with UNMISS support accepted; arms flows and external interference addressed in OP6/OP7 but not as a separate operative paragraph.
replies.Panama: accepted: OP2(e) includes women, youth and civil society; OP4 includes SOFA and UNMISS freedom of movement.
replies.Republic of Korea: partially accepted: OP4 SOFA/flight clearances and OP6 arms embargo included; OP3 requires reporting on the investigation outcome but does not require public release.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: sovereignty, consent and SOFA reflected and PP6 qualified; retained robust action and independent accountability/reporting.
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: OP3 includes UN support and reporting; OP7 includes investigation, arms flows and displacement; civil society included.
replies.Slovenia: accepted: OP3 investigation/reporting, children violations in OP2(c), and arms-transfer prevention in OP6 included.
replies.Somalia: partially accepted: coordination with the Government, AU and IGAD and reporting consultation included; investigation language adjusted with UN support and all-party cooperation.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: OP3 UNMISS-supported investigation, OP4 SOFA/movement restrictions, OP6 arms embargo compliance and OP5 civic space included.

steps.summary: The revised text extends UNMISS for one year, strengthens accountability and humanitarian access, and incorporates host-state and regional concerns to secure broad support. It maintains a robust protection-of-civilians mandate while accommodating key permanent-member sensitivities.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the penholder for revising the text to reflect key concerns on South Sudan’s sovereignty and primary responsibility, close coordination with the Government, the African Union and IGAD, and continuous review of the sanctions regime, including the arms embargo. The current text provides a balanced basis for renewing UNMISS and supporting South Sudanese-led peace efforts. Algeria therefore supports the text as it stands and will vote in favour.
messages.China: China supports the revised draft and appreciates the incorporation of its concerns on sovereignty, consent, host-State ownership and non-interference. We call on all parties to cooperate with UNMISS and to respect the Status of Forces Agreement, and China will vote in favour of the text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the revised draft and welcomes the incorporation of our key concerns on accountability and evidence preservation, women's full, equal and meaningful participation, and arms-embargo compliance and reporting. We are ready to vote in favour and encourage the Council to speak with one voice in support of UNMISS and the protection of civilians in South Sudan.
messages.France: France supports the current text and thanks the United States for incorporating our earlier concerns on access, accountability, arms flows and regional impact. We believe the draft provides a robust mandate for UNMISS and sends a clear message on protection of civilians, humanitarian access and respect for the Status of Forces Agreement. France calls on all Council members to unite behind this text and on the parties to implement it fully and without delay.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft as a balanced and timely renewal of UNMISS's mandate. We welcome the strong language on the attack on the MSF hospital, humanitarian access, accountability and full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement. Given that the current mandate expires tomorrow, we urge all members to join consensus and adopt the text without delay.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for incorporating our key concerns, including an independent and impartial investigation with UNMISS support and reporting on arms flows and external interference. We support the revised text and will vote in favour of the renewal of UNMISS. We urge all parties to respect the Status of Forces Agreement, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and protect civilians and medical personnel.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the revised draft and welcomes that it anchors UNMISS’s mandate in respect for South Sudan’s sovereignty, host-government consent and close coordination with the African Union and IGAD. We also value the balanced language on sanctions review and on the need for verifiable information regarding cross-border movements. Pakistan will vote in favour and encourages the Council to maintain consensus.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the current text and welcomes the incorporation of our earlier requests on OP2(e) and OP4, including the strengthened language on inclusive participation and UNMISS freedom of movement. We believe the draft provides a balanced mandate focused on protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability and respect for South Sudan’s sovereignty, and we are ready to support it as it stands.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating the SOFA and flight-clearance language in OP4 and the arms-embargo language in OP6. We continue to believe that accountability is strengthened by transparency and therefore request that OP3 require the investigation’s findings to be made public, as appropriate, while protecting victims and witnesses, and reported to the Council. With that change, we are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Russian Federation: We note that the penholder has reflected sovereignty, consent and the Status of Forces Agreement, and has qualified language on cross-border movements. However, the text still contains provisions on robust action, independent accountability and arms-related reporting that exceed the mandate and prejudice the Government of South Sudan. We can support the resolution if these remaining concerns are addressed; otherwise we will be compelled to abstain.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft, which reflects our priorities on protection of civilians, accountability, humanitarian access and inclusive political participation. We welcome the accepted improvements on UN support and reporting for the investigation, reporting on arms flows and cross-border displacement, and the inclusion of civil society. We urge all Council members to support a unified renewal of UNMISS and to ensure full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the revised draft and welcomes the inclusion of our priorities on accountability for the Old Fangak hospital attack, grave violations against children, and preventing arms transfers that fuel the conflict. We urge all Council members to unite behind this text and call on all parties to implement it fully, especially on protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the revised draft text, which reflects the key principles of host-State consent, sovereignty, and close coordination with the African Union and IGAD. We have no further changes to request and will vote in favour. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice in renewing UNMISS.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the current text. We welcome the inclusion of robust language on the attack on the MSF hospital, UNMISS freedom of movement, compliance with the arms embargo and civic space. We encourage all Council members to unite in renewing UNMISS's mandate and to ensure its full implementation.

replies.Republic of Korea: accepted: public reporting of investigation findings strengthens accountability while protecting victims and witnesses.
replies.Russian Federation: rejected: the proposed changes would weaken UNMISS's protection mandate, independent accountability, and arms-embargo reporting.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria has consistently supported UNMISS mandate renewals and the draft incorporates its priorities on sovereignty, consent, AU/IGAD coordination, and sanctions review. It condemns the hospital strike and calls for accountability, so a yes vote with a pre-vote explanation is consistent with its record.
reasons.China: China supports UNMISS renewal because the draft includes key sovereignty and host-government consent language and does not impose new sanctions. Beijing can back the US text while emphasizing civilian protection, political dialogue, and regional ownership.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark has consistently supported UNMISS mandate renewals and the draft aligns with its commitments to civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, and regional peace efforts. No specific concerns were raised in the last negotiation round, so no explanation before the vote is needed.
reasons.France: France has consistently supported UNMISS mandate renewals and robust civilian protection, humanitarian access and accountability language. The draft aligns with France’s priorities and there is no reason to abstain or vote against.
reasons.Greece: Greece has consistently supported the renewal of UNMISS and voted in favour of the prior US-penholder resolutions on this file. The draft aligns with Greece’s emphasis on international humanitarian law, accountability, humanitarian access, sovereignty and multilateral cooperation with regional organizations.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported UNMISS mandate renewals and the draft reflects its A3+ priorities on sovereignty, humanitarian protection, accountability, and AU/IGAD coordination. The resolution is therefore consistent with Guyana’s established position.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan has consistently supported UNMISS mandate renewals and South Sudan stability, and the draft contains Pakistan-friendly language on sovereignty, consent, AU/IGAD coordination, and humanitarian access. It also condemns the hospital attack and calls for accountability, consistent with Pakistan’s support for civilian protection while allowing it to voice sanctions-review concerns.
reasons.Panama: Panama has consistently supported UNMISS mandate renewals and the United States penholder, and this draft aligns with Panama’s priorities on civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, and sovereignty. Panama recorded support in the last negotiation round and made no requested changes.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported UNMISS mandate renewals and accountability measures, and its requested change on public reporting was accepted. Voting in favour aligns with its stated priorities on civilian protection, humanitarian access, and compliance with the arms embargo.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has repeatedly abstained on US-penholder South Sudan drafts and its key amendments on sovereignty, “robust action,” accountability and arms-embargo reporting were rejected. A veto of a UNMISS renewal would be disproportionate, so abstention is the most consistent position.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported UNMISS renewal, protection of civilians, humanitarian access and accountability, and the draft reflects key A3+ concerns on sovereignty, AU/IGAD coordination and sanctions review. It therefore votes in favour and does not need to take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has consistently supported UNMISS renewals and civilian-protection mandates, and the draft aligns with its priorities on humanitarian access, accountability and inclusive political processes.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia has consistently supported UNMISS renewals and the draft aligns with its priorities on sovereignty, civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, and African-led peace efforts. It therefore votes in favour and explains its support before the vote.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom has consistently supported UNMISS renewal and the draft reflects UK priorities on civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability and compliance with the Status of Forces Agreement. As a permanent member and strong supporter of the mission, the UK would vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is the penholder and has consistently supported UNMISS renewals; the draft reflects core U.S. priorities on humanitarian access, accountability, and South Sudan-led peace implementation, so Washington votes yes and explains its support.

before.Algeria: Thank you, Mr. President. Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because the renewal of UNMISS is urgent and necessary to protect civilians, facilitate unhindered humanitarian access, monitor human rights violations, and support South Sudanese-led implementation of the Revitalised Agreement. We welcome that the text affirms respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan, and that it provides for the Mission to act with the consent of and in close consultation with the Government of South Sudan, in accordance with the Status of Forces Agreement. We also welcome the recognition of the important role of the African Union and IGAD and the need for complementarity with regional efforts. Algeria strongly condemns the airstrike on the Médecins Sans Frontières hospital in Old Fangak and all attacks on civilians and civilian objects, and we call for a prompt, transparent, independent and impartial investigation and accountability. We reiterate that the South Sudan sanctions regime, including the arms embargo, must remain under continuous review, including with a view to adjusting it as appropriate in support of the implementation of the Revitalised Agreement and the development of national security capacity, without prejudice to South Sudan’s sovereignty. We call on all parties to cease hostilities, respect international humanitarian law, ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and refrain from actions that fuel the conflict. Algeria remains committed to a South Sudanese-led and South Sudanese-owned political process, with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society.
before.China: China supports the renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Mission in the Republic of South Sudan. We welcome the draft’s reaffirmation of the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan, and its emphasis on the consent of and close consultation with the Government of South Sudan. China calls on all parties to cease hostilities, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and conduct a prompt, independent and impartial investigation into the attack on the hospital in Old Fangak. We support South Sudanese-led political dialogue and the important role of the African Union and IGAD. China will vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this resolution. The situation in South Sudan remains deeply alarming, and the attack on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak is unacceptable. UNMISS must be able to fulfil its protection, human rights and humanitarian tasks, including through full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement and unhindered access. France also stresses the need for accountability, implementation of the Revitalised Agreement, inclusive preparations for credible elections, respect for the sovereignty of South Sudan and the Sudan, and full compliance with the arms embargo. We call on all parties to cease hostilities and protect civilians.
before.Greece: Greece will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn the airstrike on the Médecins Sans Frontières hospital in Old Fangak and all attacks on civilians and civilian objects, and we call for a prompt, independent and transparent investigation with full accountability. Greece supports the renewal of UNMISS’s mandate, including its protection of civilians, humanitarian access, human rights monitoring and good offices roles, in full respect for South Sudan’s sovereignty and in close cooperation with the Government of South Sudan, the African Union and IGAD. We underscore the need for full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement, unimpeded humanitarian access, and a South Sudanese-led political process with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society.
before.Guyana: Thank you, Mr. President. Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because the renewal of UNMISS is essential to protecting civilians, facilitating lifesaving humanitarian access and supporting South Sudan’s path toward peace and credible political preparations. Guyana condemns in the strongest terms the airstrike on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak and all attacks on civilians and civilian objects, and we underscore the need for a prompt, independent and transparent investigation, with full accountability. We also stress that all parties must fully respect the Status of Forces Agreement and allow safe, rapid and unhindered access for UNMISS and humanitarian actors. Guyana remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan, and to a South Sudanese-led process, with close coordination among the United Nations, the African Union and IGAD. We further call for full compliance with the arms embargo and for efforts to prevent arms flows that fuel the conflict. Guyana supports this mandate renewal and will continue to stand with the people of South Sudan in their pursuit of peace, justice and stability.
before.Pakistan: Thank you, Mr. President. Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of UNMISS and its important role in protecting civilians, facilitating humanitarian access, monitoring human rights, and supporting South Sudanese-led peace efforts. We strongly condemn the attack on the Médecins Sans Frontières hospital in Old Fangak and all attacks on civilians and civilian objects, and we call for a prompt, independent and transparent investigation, with full accountability. At the same time, the mandate must be implemented in full respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan, and in close consultation with the Government of South Sudan in accordance with the Status of Forces Agreement. Pakistan also values the resolution’s recognition of the role of the African Union and IGAD and the need for complementarity with South Sudanese-owned processes. We stress that sanctions regimes should remain under periodic review and must not prejudge future decisions of the Council. Pakistan remains committed to peace and stability in South Sudan and the region.
before.Panama: Panama thanks the United States for its penholdership and the constructive consultations on this draft. Panama will vote in favour. The renewal of UNMISS is essential to protect civilians, facilitate safe and unhindered humanitarian access, monitor and report human rights violations and abuses, and support the implementation of the Revitalised Agreement and credible electoral preparations. We strongly condemn the airstrike on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak and all attacks on civilians and civilian objects, and we stress the need for a prompt, independent investigation and accountability. We also underline the importance of full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement, compliance with the arms embargo, and close coordination with the African Union and IGAD, in full respect of the sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the extension of UNMISS’s mandate and the strengthened provisions on protection of civilians, humanitarian access, human rights monitoring and accountability, including the independent investigation into the attack on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak. We appreciate that the penholder accepted our proposal for the Secretary-General to make public the findings of that investigation, as appropriate and consistent with the protection of victims and witnesses. We also stress the importance of full respect for South Sudan’s sovereignty, the Status of Forces Agreement, the arms embargo, and South Sudanese-led political dialogue with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society, in close coordination with the African Union and IGAD. The Republic of Korea remains committed to supporting the people of South Sudan and the Council’s efforts to advance peace, stability and accountability.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will abstain on this draft resolution. We support the continued presence of UNMISS and the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and we unequivocally condemn the attack on the hospital in Old Fangak. However, the draft retains language that expands the Mission’s mandate in sensitive areas without sufficient regard for the sovereignty and primary responsibility of the Government of South Sudan. It also fails to reflect in full our proposals on national ownership of accountability efforts, independent investigation by national authorities, and balanced reporting on arms-related issues. Our abstention is not indifference to the situation in South Sudan. We call for strict respect for sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-interference, and close coordination with the African Union and IGAD. The authors could and should have reflected these principles more fully.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the United States for its leadership and will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the extension of UNMISS’s mandate and its vital role in protecting civilians, facilitating safe and unhindered humanitarian access, monitoring human rights, and supporting the implementation of the Revitalised Agreement. Slovenia strongly condemns the airstrike on the Médecins Sans Frontières hospital in Old Fangak and all attacks on civilians and civilian objects, and we call for a prompt, independent and impartial investigation and accountability. We underline that UNMISS must be able to move freely and that the Government of South Sudan must fully respect the Status of Forces Agreement. A sustainable solution requires inclusive political dialogue and credible preparations for elections, with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society. Slovenia remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan and to the protection of all civilians.
before.Somalia: Thank you, Mr. President. Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of UNMISS’s mandate, including its critical role in protecting civilians, facilitating humanitarian access, monitoring human rights, and supporting accountability. We stress the need for full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan and for the primary responsibility of the Government of South Sudan, in close coordination with the African Union and IGAD. We condemn in the strongest terms the attack on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak and call for a prompt, independent investigation and accountability. We also urge all parties to ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access and to pursue an inclusive, South Sudanese-led political dialogue and credible preparations for elections, with the full and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. We thank the United States for its leadership and welcome the extension of UNMISS’s mandate, which is essential for protecting civilians and supporting humanitarian access across South Sudan. We strongly condemn the appalling airstrike on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak and all attacks on civilians and civilian objects, and we call for a prompt, transparent, independent and impartial investigation with full accountability. We urge all parties to cease hostilities, respect international humanitarian law, and allow safe and unhindered access for UNMISS and humanitarian actors. We also call on the Government of South Sudan to respect fully the Status of Forces Agreement, on all parties to implement the Revitalised Agreement, and on all Member States to comply with the arms embargo and refrain from actions that fuel the conflict.
before.United States of America: The United States thanks Council members for their engagement on this urgent renewal. UNMISS’s work protecting civilians, facilitating lifesaving humanitarian access, and supporting implementation of the Revitalised Agreement remains essential, especially after the horrific attack on the MSF hospital in Old Fangak. The resolution before us renews the mandate, calls for accountability and full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement, and reinforces the need for a South Sudanese-led political process. We urge all members to vote in favour.

after.Denmark: Thank you, Mr. President. Denmark voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its adoption. The renewal of UNMISS is essential to protect civilians, facilitate safe and unhindered humanitarian access, monitor human rights violations and abuses, and support South Sudan’s implementation of the Revitalised Agreement. Denmark strongly condemns the airstrike on the Médecins Sans Frontières hospital in Old Fangak and all attacks on civilians and civilian objects. Those responsible must be held accountable through a prompt, transparent, independent and impartial investigation. We call on all parties to cease hostilities, respect international humanitarian law, and fully respect the Status of Forces Agreement so that UNMISS can implement its mandate. We also stress the importance of inclusive, South Sudanese-led political dialogue and credible preparations for elections, with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society, in full respect for South Sudan’s sovereignty. Denmark further underscores the need for full compliance with the arms embargo and close coordination with the African Union and IGAD. Denmark will continue to support the people of South Sudan and efforts to ensure accountability and lasting peace.
after.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr. President. Sierra Leone voted in favour of this resolution because the renewal of UNMISS is urgent and indispensable. The Mission’s protection of civilians, facilitation of safe and unhindered humanitarian access, human rights monitoring and support for the implementation of the Revitalised Agreement remain central to preventing further suffering and supporting a South Sudanese-led peace process. We welcome the text’s reaffirmation of the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan, and its recognition that UNMISS acts with the consent of and in close consultation with the Government of South Sudan, in accordance with the Status of Forces Agreement. At the same time, we strongly condemn the airstrike on the Médecins Sans Frontières hospital in Old Fangak and all attacks on civilians and civilian objects. Such attacks are unacceptable. We call for a prompt, transparent, independent and impartial investigation, and for those responsible to be held accountable. All parties must respect international humanitarian law and human rights law, ensure safe, rapid and unhindered access for UNMISS and humanitarian actors, and fully respect the Status of Forces Agreement. Sierra Leone also underscores the importance of close coordination and complementarity with the African Union and IGAD, and of inclusive political dialogue and credible electoral preparations with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society. We remain concerned at the regional impact of the conflict in the Sudan, including cross-border displacement and reports of arms flows, and we stress the need for verifiable information and full compliance with the sanctions regime. Sierra Leone will continue to support the Council’s efforts to protect civilians and to stand with the people of South Sudan in their pursuit of peace and stability. Thank you.
after.United States of America: The United States welcomes the adoption of this resolution. We thank Council members for their broad support and for engaging constructively on a text that renews UNMISS’s vital mandate and sends a clear message that attacks on civilians and medical facilities in South Sudan must stop and be investigated and that those responsible must be held accountable. The United States remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of South Sudan. We call on all parties to respect the Status of Forces Agreement, allow safe and unhindered humanitarian access, cease hostilities, and support a South Sudanese-led political process. The Council has spoken with one voice, and we expect the resolution’s provisions to be implemented fully and without delay.
